proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu=P_{M_0}\) and \(\nu=P_{M_1}\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak R(H,L)\) supplies the refinement-span, instantaneous-acyclicity, and exact-summary conditions.  The remaining hypotheses supply the fixed finite alphabet, semi-Markovianity, time homogeneity, strict stationarity, and cylinder positivity.  Thus, by \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\),
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A).
\]

We prove carefully that equality on every finite cylinder implies equality of the entire process measures.  Let \(\mathscr E\) be the algebra of finite unions of cylinders in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Any finite collection of cylinders can be refined to the atoms on the union of its finite coordinate supports.  Therefore equality of \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) on cylinders implies equality on \(\mathscr E\).

For completeness, here is the measure-uniqueness argument rather than an undeclared appeal to it.  Let \(\mathscr D\) be the smallest lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\).  For \(A\in\mathscr E\), the class \(\mathscr D_A=\{B:A\cap B\in\mathscr D\}\) is a lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\), so \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr D_A\).  Repeating the argument with \(A\in\mathscr D\) shows that \(\mathscr D\) is closed under finite intersections.  A lambda-system closed under finite intersections is a sigma-field; hence \(\mathscr D=\sigma(\mathscr E)\), the product sigma-field.  Now let
\[
 \mathscr C=\{B:\mu(A\cap B)=\nu(A\cap B)\text{ for every }A\in\mathscr E\}.
\]
Finite-measure additivity shows directly that \(\mathscr C\) is a lambda-system.  Since \(\mu=\nu\) on \(\mathscr E\), the algebra \(\mathscr E\) is contained in \(\mathscr C\).  Thus \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr C\).  Taking \(A=\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) yields \(\mu(B)=\nu(B)\) for every product-measurable \(B\), and therefore \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

The assumed inequality
\[
 \theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)
\]
together with this whole-law equality violates the implication in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\).  Consequently \(\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=0\).  No alphabet enlargement or auxiliary edge channel is used: the lemma only verifies a pair of final fixed-alphabet SCMs constructed directly by a rejecting branch.

Every directed edge of \(G^\star\) goes from time \(t-\ell\) to time \(t\) with \(0\le\ell\le L\).  Projecting a directed path in \(G^\star\) to coordinate labels gives a directed walk in the directed part of \(H\).  Because that graph is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, no coordinate can repeat.  A directed path into either query vertex therefore has at most \(n-1\) edges and total backward displacement at most \((n-1)L\).  Hence
\[
 A^\star:=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})
 \subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0].
\]
The interval has \(\gamma+(n-1)L+1\le nL+1\) integer times because \(0\le\gamma\le L\), so
\[
 |A^\star|\le n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\le n(nL+1).
\]

Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with refinement \(R\).  Exact-summary compatibility and the refinement-span condition imply \(R\subseteq G^\star\).  Since \(A^\star\) is ancestral in \(G^\star\), no directed arrow from an observed vertex outside \(A^\star\) enters it.  Removing outside observed vertices therefore leaves all structural equations on \(A^\star\) unchanged.  A pairwise exogenous root with only one endpoint remaining becomes a private root, so the marginal law on \(A^\star\) is generated by a semi-Markovian SCM compatible with the supergraph \(G^\star[A^\star]\).

If ordinary ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{lem:ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 F(P_M(A^\star))
 =P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\theta_M(y;x).
\]
The set \(A^\star\) is finite.  Thus each joint or marginal cell in the returned expression is a finite cylinder probability on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Finite-alphabet marginalization uses finite sums, district factorization uses finite products, and every conditional-kernel denominator is positive by cylinder positivity.  Therefore \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\).  Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the equality is uniform over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).  This proves only the soundness direction; an ID failure in the saturated graph is not converted into a fixed-alphabet stationary countermodel.

Put \(A_t=O_{1,t}\), \(B_t=O_{2,t}\), and \(C_t=O_{3,t}\), and for \(s\in(0,1)\) define \(b_s(d)=s^d(1-s)^{1-d}\), \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  All variables are binary by \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\).  The two-sided structural solutions exist and are unique causal functions of the noise histories.  Indeed, model zero obeys
\[
 B_t=(R_t\wedge B_{t-1})\oplus U_t\oplus N_t,
\]
and model one obeys
\[
 A_t=(R'_t\wedge A_{t-1})\oplus U'_t\oplus N'_t.
\]
Whenever \(R_t=0\), respectively \(R'_t=0\), the right side forgets the preceding state.  Such reset times occur infinitely often backward almost surely because the reset indicators are independent with probability \(1/2\).  Starting at the most recent reset before \(t\) defines the state at \(t\), and any two causal solutions agree after that reset.  This construction commutes with integer time shifts.

In model zero, conditional on the complete observed past, \(U_t\) is an independent fair bit.  Hence, for \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})
 &=P_{M_0}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})P_{M_0}(N_t=a\oplus b)\\
 &=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, the same argument makes \(B_t\) conditionally fair and \(A_t=B_t\oplus N'_t\), so
\[
 P_{M_1}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
Thus in either model \((A_t,B_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is an independent sequence with common mass
\[
 \pi(a,b)=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
Moreover, in both models,
\[
 P(C_t=c\mid(A_s,B_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z},(C_s)_{s<t})=b_r(c\oplus B_{t-1}).
\]
Both observed processes therefore admit the same representation: draw the pairs \((A_t,B_t)\) independently with mass \(\pi\), draw \(E_t\) independently with success probability \(r\), and set \(C_t=B_{t-1}\oplus E_t\).  For a complete cylinder on an interval \([u,v]\), its probability is
\[
 \sum_{b_{u-1}\in\{0,1\}}\frac12
 \prod_{t=u}^{v}\pi(a_t,b_t)b_r(c_t\oplus b_{t-1}),
\]
with summation over any unspecified cells.  The formula is identical for both models and invariant under translating \([u,v]\).  Hence the laws agree on every cylinder, are strictly stationary, and, by the cylinder-uniqueness argument in \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\), agree as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Since \(q=1/5\) and \(r=1/10\), all factors are positive; marginalization then gives positivity of every finite cylinder.

The structural functions also verify exact graph membership.  In model zero, the active directed edges are \(B_{t-1}\to A_t\), \(A_t\to B_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  In model one, they are \(A_{t-1}\to B_t\), \(B_t\to A_t\), and \(B_{t-1}\to C_t\).  Each instantaneous slice contains only one of \(A_t\to B_t\) and \(B_t\to A_t\), hence is acyclic.  All primitive noises are mutually independent, so no bidirected edge is present.  The equations are time homogeneous, and every directed lag is at most one.  Both exact summaries are consequently \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), and \(2\to3\), with no bidirected edge.  Finite binary support, semi-Markovianity, stationarity, and positivity now give
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A).
\]

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0)\) in model zero,
\[
 B_{-1}=N_{-1},\qquad C_0=N_{-1}\oplus E_0.
\]
Independence yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 &=q(1-r)+(1-q)r\\
 &=q+r-2qr=\frac15+\frac1{10}-\frac2{50}=\frac{13}{50}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, \(A_{-1}\) is a child of the fair variable \(B_{-1}\), which is the only observed parent of \(C_0\).  Intervention on \(A_{-1}\) leaves \(B_{-1}\) fair, and therefore
\[
 P_{M_1}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 =\frac12(1-r)+\frac12r=\frac12.
\]
Each effect is separately identifiable in its known refinement.  In model zero it equals
\[
 \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}P(C_0=1\mid B_{-1}=b)P(B_{-1}=b\mid A_{-1}=0),
\]
because the graph has no hidden common cause and its relevant directed path is \(A_{-1}\to B_{-1}\to C_0\).  In model one there is no directed path from \(A_{-1}\) to \(C_0\), so the effect is \(P(C_0=1)\).  Cylinder positivity makes both functionals well defined.  This proves the claimed fixed-alphabet, whole-law collision and its exact arithmetic.

Write
\[
 N_\star=n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}.
\]
All preliminary branch tests in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) compare finite graphs, finite alphabets, and fixed query labels.  In the acyclic branch, \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) places the ancestral graph on at most \(N_\star\) vertices.  A memoized ID subproblem labels every such vertex as absent, random, or fixed.  There are at most \(3^{N_\star}\) labels, and memoization makes every label visited at most once.  Including initialization and the three ordered branch tests gives at most
\[
 4+3^{N_\star}=B_\star(n,L,\gamma)
\]
transitions.  Thus the procedure terminates within the asserted bound and, because the branches are ordered and deterministic, emits exactly one of the three tags.

For the first branch, \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\) proves that \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) equals the causal query for every compatible model.  For an acyclic-branch ID success, \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) proves that the returned \(F\) is in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and equals \(\theta_M(y;x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).  These are the only success branches, so success soundness follows.

The sole failure branch emits the rational structural tables and noise probabilities of \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}collision}\) proves directly that these tables define \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A)\), that their entire observed laws coincide, and that their target values are \(13/50\) and \(1/2\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\), in its corrected direct-certificate form, then certifies \(\operatorname{UID}=0\) without changing the alphabets.  This proves failure soundness.

If the procedure succeeds, any two compatible models with the same process law give the same values to all cylinders in \(F\), hence the same value of \(F\), and therefore the same target value.  By \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\), success implies \(\operatorname{UID}=1\).  If it fails, the displayed pair violates that defining implication, so failure implies \(\operatorname{UID}=0\).  The procedure deliberately returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) in all remaining cases.  Accordingly neither converse is asserted, and the original sound-and-complete dichotomy does not follow.

For \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the coordinate set is \(V=\{X,Y\}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\) requires a nonempty set
\[
 \mathcal D\subseteq(V\setminus\{X,Y\})\times[-b,0].
\]
The right side is empty, so \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)=\varnothing\).  By the first ordered branch of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\), the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\) on this exact input.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\) gives, for every compatible \(M\),
\[
 F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
 =P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0)).
\]
Thus the certified procedure has a successful input outside the defined front-door family.  The proof neither maps every certificate to a transducer trace nor claims that Assaad's published criterion is embedded; those parts of the former statement required an unspecified \(F_c\) and unspecified transitions and have been removed.

On the event \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), success soundness in \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) gives the load-bearing identifying equality
\[
 F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).  All remaining hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\) are exactly \(\mathrm{ass:strict\text{-}stationarity}\), \(\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\), \(\mathrm{ass:geometric\text{-}beta\text{-}mixing}\), \(\mathrm{ass:hac\text{-}kernel}\), \(\mathrm{ass:hac\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}nondegeneracy}\).  Applying that lemma yields HAC consistency, the centered delta-method limit, consistency of \(\widehat v_F\), Wald coverage, and representation invariance exactly as stated.  The arbitrary off-domain definition in that lemma is immaterial because the empirical denominators are positive with probability tending to one.

If \(L=0\), then \(\gamma=0\).  Refinement span permits only lag-zero directed and shared-root relations.  Exact summary fixes their coordinate pairs to those in \(H\), and instantaneous acyclicity makes the directed part of \(H\) a DAG without a directed self-loop.  The ordered procedure therefore reaches its acyclic branch and its ancestral ADMG is the ordinary finite static ancestral graph for the query \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\).  It invokes exactly the memoized ordinary ID call specified in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\).  If ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) proves that \(F\) is the ordinary ID functional and is uniformly valid on the common product alphabet.  If ID fails, the procedure returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) by construction.  No static hedge is claimed to lift to a positive stationary pair on every fixed alphabet.

For every successful query, \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) proves that the returned cylinder functional equals the causal target throughout the compatible class.  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}margin\text{-}plugin\text{-}ranking}\) to the fixed finite collection of successful functionals shows that, under the stated sampling assumptions and positive population margin, their plug-in ordering is correct with probability tending to one.  The failure branch is sound by the same theorem and carries the explicit lag-switch pair; the unknown branch makes no causal assertion.  Excluding both tags from ranking therefore assigns scores only where a uniform identifying functional has been proved.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite acyclic directed mixed graph \(\mathcal G\), whenever the recursive ID algorithm returns an expression for \(P_{\mathbf x}(\mathbf y)\), that expression equals the interventional distribution in every semi-Markovian SCM compatible with \(\mathcal G\).

source.verbatim_statement: Whenever ID returns an expression for \(P_{\mathbf{x}}(\mathbf{y})\), it is correct.

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 38 in the JMLR publisher PDF.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the input \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)\) is empty, while for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\),
\[
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
 =F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
 =\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=0,X_0=a)P_M(X_0=a).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Here \(V=\{X,Y\}\), so the required nonempty mediator set in \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\) cannot exist.  Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Exact summary says that the only possible observed parents of \(Y_0\) are \(X_{-1}\) and \(X_0\), with at least one of those arguments active, and that \(X_t\) has no observed parent.  There is no bidirected summary edge.  By semi-Markovianity the root of \(Y_0\) is independent of the distinct roots generating \(X_{-1}\) and \(X_0\), and those latter roots are independent of one another.  Define
\[
 g(u,v)=P_M\{f_Y(u,v,U_{Y,0})=1\},
\]
omitting an argument if its lag is absent.  Exogenous independence and cylinder positivity imply
\[
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=u,X_0=v)=g(u,v).
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0)\), the variable \(X_0\) and root \(U_{Y,0}\) retain their observational laws.  The truncated structural equations and the law of total probability give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
 &=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}g(0,a)P_M(X_0=a)\\
 &=\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}P_M(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=0,X_0=a)P_M(X_0=a)\\
 &=F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every displayed conditional has positive denominator by cylinder positivity.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\mathcal A\) and \(M\), and let \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) use finitely many cylinders.  Assume \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\), strict stationarity, cylinder positivity, \(\beta_M(k)\le C_\beta\rho^k\), the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).  Define \(\widehat\theta_F\) and \(\widehat v_F\) on the event that their empirical denominators are positive, and arbitrarily off that event.  Then that event has probability tending to one,
\[
 \widehat\Omega_F\overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F,\qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x))\Rightarrow N(0,v_F),\qquad
 \widehat v_F\overset p\longrightarrow v_F,
\]
and
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
Algebraically equivalent cylinder expressions have the same limit after redundant simplex coordinates are removed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \([a_j,b_j]\) be the smallest integer interval containing the time indices in cylinder \(j\), after placing that cylinder at shift zero, and put \(w=\max_j(b_j-a_j)<\infty\).  The vector \(Z_t\) is measurable with respect to a finite observed block of width at most \(w\).  For \(k>w\), restriction of sigma-fields in the definition of absolute regularity gives
\[
 \beta_Z(k)\le\beta_M(k-w)\le C_\beta\rho^{k-w},
\]
while \(\beta_Z(k)\le1\) for the finitely many \(k\le w\).  Since each coordinate of \(Z_t\) lies in \([0,1]\), the total-variation definition of \(\beta\) gives, for bounded scalar functions \(G,H\) of blocks separated by \(k\),
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}(G,H)|
 \le4\lVert G\rVert_\infty\lVert H\rVert_\infty\beta_Z(k).
\]
Consequently every entry of \(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Cov}(Z_0,Z_k)\) is absolutely summable, \(\Omega_F\) is finite, and
\[
 E\lVert\widehat p_F-p_F\rVert^2=O(T^{-1}).
\]
Omitting the fixed boundary required by the cylinders changes the mean by \(O(T^{-1})\), so \(\widehat p_F-p_F=O_p(T^{-1/2})\).

We derive the required multivariate central limit theorem by blocking.  Fix \(c\) and put \(W_t=c^{\mathsf T}(Z_t-p_F)\).  Let \(b_T=\lfloor T^{1/5}\rfloor\), let \(s_T=\lceil d\log T\rceil\) with \(d>2/|\log\rho|\), and partition \(1,\ldots,T\) into big blocks of length \(b_T\) separated by gaps of length \(s_T\).  Absolute covariance summability shows that the variance of the gap sum divided by \(T\) is \(O(s_T/b_T)=o(1)\).  If \(m_T\) is the number of big blocks, iterative use of the total-variation definition bounds the difference between their joint characteristic function and the product of their marginal characteristic functions by
\[
 2(m_T-1)\beta_Z(s_T)
 \le C\frac{T}{b_T}\rho^{s_T-w}=o(1).
\]
It remains to analyze independent variables with the big-block-sum marginals.  Absolute covariance summability gives
\[
 \frac1T\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\right)
 \longrightarrow \sigma_c^2:=c^{\mathsf T}\Omega_Fc,
\]
and removing the gaps preserves this limit.  Each centered big-block sum is bounded by \(Cb_T\).  Taylor expansion of its characteristic function has total third-order remainder at most
\[
 \frac{Cb_T}{T^{3/2}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_T}\operatorname{Var}(B_{T,j})
 =O(b_TT^{-1/2})=o(1).
\]
The quadratic terms converge to \(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2\), while their maximum is \(O(b_T/T)=o(1)\).  Their product therefore converges to \(\exp(-u^2\sigma_c^2/2)\).  Restoring the negligible gaps proves
\[
 T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^T W_t\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma_c^2).
\]
Because \(c\) was arbitrary, the characteristic-function identity yields
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_F).
\]

For HAC consistency, write \(U_t=Z_t-p_F\), \(\Gamma_k=E(U_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T})\), and
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_k=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^TU_tU_{t-k}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For any matrix entry, products indexed by \(t\) and \(t+r\) are bounded.  If \(r>k+w\), their observed blocks are separated by at least \(r-k-w\), so the covariance inequality applies; for the remaining \(k+w+1\) separations use the bound by one.  Uniformly for \(0\le k<T\),
\[
 E\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\sqrt{\frac{k+w+1}{T}}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 E\sum_{k=0}^{h_T}\lVert\widetilde\Gamma_k-E\widetilde\Gamma_k\rVert
 \le C\frac{h_T^{3/2}}{\sqrt T}=o(1),
\]
because \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).  Also \(E\widetilde\Gamma_k=(1-k/T)\Gamma_k\).  The Bartlett weights converge to one at each fixed lag and are bounded by one.  Since \(\sum_k\lVert\Gamma_k\rVert<\infty\), truncating first at a fixed lag and then sending that lag to infinity gives
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_0+
 \sum_{k=1}^{h_T}K(k/(h_T+1))
 (\widetilde\Gamma_k+\widetilde\Gamma_k^{\mathsf T})
 \overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F.
\]
With \(d_T=\widehat p_F-p_F\), replacing \(U_t\) by \(U_t-d_T\) changes each empirical lag covariance by at most \(C(\lVert d_T\rVert+\lVert d_T\rVert^2)\).  Summing through \(h_T\) gives \(O_p(h_TT^{-1/2})=o_p(1)\).  Thus \(\widehat\Omega_F\overset p\to\Omega_F\).

Every denominator of \(F\) is positive at \(p_F\).  Since there are finitely many denominators, they remain positive on a neighborhood of \(p_F\).  Consistency of \(\widehat p_F\) makes the empirical-domain event have probability tending to one.  On this neighborhood the rational map is twice continuously differentiable, and Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt T\{F(\widehat p_F)-F(p_F)\}
 =\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\sqrt T(\widehat p_F-p_F)+o_p(1).
\]
Using \(F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)\) yields the stated normal limit with
\[
 v_F=\nabla F(p_F)^{\mathsf T}\Omega_F\nabla F(p_F).
\]
Continuity of \(\nabla F\), consistency of \(\widehat p_F\), and HAC consistency imply \(\widehat v_F\to_pv_F\).  Because \(v_F>0\), studentization gives the asserted Wald coverage.

Finally, remove linearly redundant cylinder cells and use coordinates on the relative interior of the resulting probability simplex.  Algebraically equivalent rational expressions agree on an open subset of those coordinates, so their gradients agree.  Before reduction, their gradient difference is normal to the affine support of \(Z_t-p_F\) and is therefore annihilated by \(\Omega_F\).  Their linear limits and quadratic variance forms coincide.

added_lemmas.statement: For a fixed finite family of valid cylinder identifying functionals \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\), suppose each trajectory obeys the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\), and let \(\theta_j=F_j(p_{F_j})\).  If \(\Delta=\min_{j\ne k}|\theta_j-\theta_k|>0\), then the ordering induced by \(\widehat\theta_{F_1},\ldots,\widehat\theta_{F_m}\) equals the population ordering with probability tending to one.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every fixed \(j\), \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\) gives \(\widehat\theta_{F_j}\to_p\theta_j\).  Since \(m<\infty\), the union bound yields
\[
 P\!\left(\max_{1\le j\le m}|\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j|\ge\Delta/3\right)
 \le\sum_{j=1}^mP\!\left(|\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j|\ge\Delta/3\right)
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
On the complementary event, \(\theta_j<\theta_k\) implies
\[
 \widehat\theta_{F_j}<\theta_j+\Delta/3
 \le\theta_k-2\Delta/3
 <\widehat\theta_{F_k}.
\]
Every pairwise comparison, and hence the full ranking, is then correct.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Fix \(\mathcal A\) satisfying \(2\le|\mathcal A_i|<\infty\) for every \(i\in V\).  Let \(M_0\) and \(M_1\) be two directly specified SCMs with refinements in \(\mathfrak R(H,L)\), observed alphabets exactly \(\mathcal A\), semi-Markovian roots, time-homogeneous equations, strictly stationary observed laws, and positive finite cylinders.  If \(P_{M_0}(C_{\mathcal A})=P_{M_1}(C_{\mathcal A})\) for every finite cylinder and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\), then \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and \(\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=0\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: A bounded offset-sensitive fixing extension that resolves every current unknown input by a common finite-cylinder functional or by two directly constructed final fixed-alphabet stationary SCMs.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available handle contains no finite state encoding, transition invariant, pumping proof, or direct fixed-alphabet model grammar for arbitrary multi-role rejection witnesses. Independent shifting assigns several roles to one coordinate-time slot or enlarges the coordinate alphabet, and per-refinement ID is refuted by the lag-switch collision.
open_obligations.attempted: The saturated ancestral ADMG gives a sound finite acyclic branch, and the explicit lag-switch tables give one direct cyclic failure. Raw quotient fixing conflates offsets; a general shift lift fails at the fixed-alphabet typing step; and no argument turns disagreement among individually identified refinements into final stationary models without unrestricted enumeration or gluing.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved partial normal form is the explicit three-way procedure in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\): it terminates within \(4+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\) transitions, returns sound finite-cylinder functionals for the outside witness and every successful saturated-ID call in the acyclic directed-summary subclass, and directly returns the positive stationary fixed-alphabet lag-switch pair with effects \(13/50\) and \(1/2\).  All other inputs return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\); resolving those inputs soundly and completely remains open.

prose_updates.tldr: The full sound-and-complete lag-robust fixing theorem is not established: a generic finite-role collision cannot be lifted by independent shifts without assigning several role values to one fixed-alphabet coordinate or enlarging that alphabet. The proved result is instead an explicit terminating three-way certified procedure. It returns a sound finite-cylinder identifying functional for the concrete outside-front-door witness and for every successful saturated ordinary-ID call when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free; it returns a direct positive stationary fixed-alphabet lag-switch countermodel pair on the verified binary collision; and it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) elsewhere. Its transition bound is \(4+3^{n(\gamma+(n-1)L+1)}\). Every success supports the cylinder plug-in estimator and modified-Bartlett HAC delta-method interval under positivity, geometric beta mixing, the stated bandwidth regime, and nonzero long-run variance. EasyRCA ranks only certified successes and distinguishes a proved failure certificate from an unresolved abstention.

project_justification.gap: Existing SCG adjustment, linear direct-effect, micro front-door, macro do-calculus, periodic-graph ID, PAG, and fixed-ADMG results do not furnish a complete nonparametric decision rule for one lag-specific micro intervention uniformly over latent-confounded stationary refinements on a fixed alphabet. In particular, fixed-graph hedges do not automatically preserve time homogeneity, exact summary, positivity, equality of the entire process law, and the unchanged coordinate alphabets under a refinement switch.
project_justification.niche: The attainable contribution is certified partial identification with graph-native abstention. Acyclic directed summaries admit a finite saturated ancestral ADMG whose successful ordinary-ID output is uniform over refinements; a separate cyclic lag-switch construction proves genuine nonidentification even though each refinement is individually identifiable. The remaining cyclic cases require the still-open offset-sensitive normal form and direct fixed-alphabet witness construction.
project_justification.fill: The explicit ordered procedure recognizes one proved outside-front-door success, one proved positive stationary lag-switch failure, and otherwise makes a memoized ordinary-ID call on at most \(n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}\) ancestral roles when the directed summary is acyclic and loop-free. It outputs \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) whenever these certified rules do not decide the query. This yields sound success and failure implications, an explicit transition bound, a concrete whole-law collision, and HAC inference, without claiming the missing converse or enlarging \(\mathcal A\).

prose_updates.related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Goessler, and Meynaoui study summary-graph total effects under causal sufficiency, while Ferreira and Assaad characterize linear direct effects under the same no-hidden-confounding boundary. Assaad gives a sufficient latent-confounded micro front-door result, and Ferreira and Assaad prove macro do-calculus completeness for interventions on whole summary clusters. None of those results supplies the direct fixed-alphabet stationary rejection construction needed for complete lag-specific micro identification. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman bound identification after a periodic fine graph is given; Jaber and coauthors decide a finite PAG class; Shpitser and Pearl prove ID soundness and completeness for one finite ADMG; and Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser develop fixing for one fixed graph. Those results motivate the finite acyclic branch but do not prove cross-refinement completeness. The present proved comparison is therefore limited: the explicit two-coordinate query lies outside the defined front-door family and is identified by a displayed cylinder functional, but no universal inclusion of that family or embedding of Assaad's criterion is claimed. Viviano and Bradic motivate beta-mixing inference, Newey and West motivate the modified-Bartlett estimator, and the note derives the required finite-window CLT, HAC consistency, and delta method for the returned cylinder probabilities.
prose_updates.interpretation: A success tag is a positive causal certificate: the displayed arithmetic functional has the same value as the lag-specific intervention probability in every compatible SCM. A failure tag is a negative causal certificate: the supplied final SCM pair has the same entire observational process law but different intervention probabilities. An unknown tag is neither; it records that the current sound rules do not decide the query. This distinction prevents an unresolved graph from being silently converted into a zero or low anomaly-transmission score.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved step is not statistical. A finite rejection witness may contain several temporal roles of the same observed coordinate. Independent-shift replication then tries to place several role values into one coordinate-time variable, while product-slot or auxiliary-channel repairs enlarge the fixed alphabet. The proved procedure avoids this defect by constructing its only failure pair directly and returning unknown elsewhere. Strict stationarity and bounded structural lag also do not make the observed process finite-order Markov, so neither transition-kernel truncation nor semantic gluing of refinement-specific formulas supplies the missing completeness proof.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves sound partial certification, not a sound-and-complete TID-SCG dichotomy. The acyclic saturated-ID branch is sound but not claimed complete for uniform identification; the static boundary returns unknown on ID failure; the front-door result is only the concrete outside-family witness; and the direct failure branch currently covers the verified binary lag-switch query. Completing all unknown cases, embedding the generic front-door family, and producing arbitrary direct fixed-alphabet countermodels remain open. The HAC theorem applies only after a sound success and additionally requires cylinder positivity, geometric beta mixing, the Bartlett kernel, \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\).
